newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela said to announce Malaysia helicopter deal.
newsitem.headline: Mandela said to announce Malaysia helicopter deal.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela, due back in South Africa on Monday after a 10-day tour of southeast Asia, is expected to announce on his return the first foreign sale of Rooivalk attack helicopters to Malaysia.
State radio said the deal to sell South Africa's state-of-the-art combat aircraft was apparently sealed last week during Mandela's talks with Malaysia's Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamed.
Rooivalk manufacturer Denel said however it knew nothing of the Malaysian deal.
"We are marketing the helicopter in many countries, including Malaysia, but we don't know of any deal yet," a Denel official told Reuters at the weekend.
Mandela's spokesman Parks Mankahlana said he was also in the dark about any agreement, but said more might become known when the president arrived back in the country at 1500 GMT.
South Africa lost a $769 million deal to sell the Rooivalk gunship to Britain last year after Pretoria could not equip the helicopter with U.S. technology because of a Washington arms embargo.

The arms embargo was, however, lifted last month after South Africa's state-owned Armscor, its subsidiary Kentron Party Ltd and a private firm, pleaded "no contest" to breaking a U.S. arms embargo which banned American military equipment exports to South Africa since 1963.
The firms were charged with smuggling munitions, restricted commodities and technology made in the United States to South Africa between 1978 and 1989, using front companies.
They were fined a total of $12.5 million.

South Africa's Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad said that Washington had agreed that all restrictions on U.S. arms companies keen to export to South Africa, and on trade in the other direction, would be lifted once the case was settled.
